newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA PRESIDENT VETOES ELECTORAL LAW AMENDMENT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA PRESIDENT VETOES ELECTORAL LAW AMENDMENT.

text.p: Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov rejected an amendment to the electoral law which lowers the barrier for parties to enter parliament to three percent from four percent of the vote.
The amendment, adopted by the outgoing parliament at its last session before being dissolved last week, paved the way for smaller parties to enter the assembly.

"I can not accept the amdendment...its consequence can be an unstable parliament, which may have difficulty in formulating a common will. This can be damaging to the country," said Stoyanov in a statement.

Stoyanov, elected on the opposition ticket in November, dissolved parliament last week in effect from February 19. The ruling Socialists agreed to opposition's demands to hold early general elections on April 19, bowing to month-long protests fueled by economic hardship.
The speaker of the outgoing parliament, convened on Tuesday the State Institutions Committee to discuss the veto.
Under Bulgarian law parliament can either accept or overturn the president's veto in plenary hall until mid-night on Tuesday, when its term expires.
If parliament fails to convene a plenary session on Tuesday evening, the previous electoral law remains in force, allowing parties to enter parliament with four percent of the vote.
Then the veto would need to be discussed by the new parliament. Parliament's press office said there were no signs of deputies meeting in plenary session so far.

"The future national assembly needs stability. It needs a common will to take important decisons which will lead Bulgaria out of its grave economic crisis, to crush unprecedented corruption and strengthen confidence in institutions," said the statement.
